stories.title: Apple TV Becomes the New U.S. Home of F1 ACADEMY in 2027
stories.summary: Apple and F1 ACADEMY have announced that the all-female racing series will stream on Apple TV in the United States beginning in 2027.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — November 19, 2026

Apple and F1 ACADEMY have announced that the all-female racing series will stream on Apple TV in the United States beginning in 2027.

Apple says fans will be able to watch every qualifying session and race throughout the season. A footnote in Apple's announcement notes that viewing requires a U.S. Apple TV subscription. F1 ACADEMY will be entering its fifth season in 2027.

F1 ACADEMY is dedicated to developing the next generation of female racing talent, creating opportunities for women on and off the track. Apple describes the move as expanding its Formula 1 coverage to spotlight that next generation and their journey through motorsport.

The announcement builds on Apple's existing Formula 1 relationship, following Apple Original Films' F1 and the five-year broadcast partnership that made Apple TV the exclusive U.S. broadcast partner for Formula 1 starting in 2026. Apple says its inaugural season of F1 coverage is now underway.

“We have built incredible momentum in the U.S., with a growing and increasingly engaged audience following our drivers and their journeys,” said Susie Wolff, F1 ACADEMY's managing director, in Apple's announcement. “Visibility remains fundamental to our mission. When young girls can switch on their screens and see women racing, competing, and succeeding, it changes what they believe is possible.”

“It's been incredible to see the excitement around Formula 1 on Apple TV, and we're thrilled to welcome F1 ACADEMY in 2027,” said Jim DeLorenzo, Apple's global head of Sports. “These talented young drivers represent the future of motorsport, and we're excited to give them a bigger platform to share their stories, inspire new fans, and bring even more great racing to viewers on Apple TV.”

Ian Holmes, Formula 1's chief media rights and broadcasting officer, added that bringing the series to Apple TV in the United States marks another step in its growth and an opportunity to inspire more women and girls to see a future for themselves in motorsport.

Per Apple, F1 ACADEMY launched in 2022 as a Formula 4-level development series and has become the second-most-followed series after Formula 1, according to the 2025 Global F1 Fan Survey. Apple names drivers including Alba Hurup Larsen, Alisha Palmowski, and Emma Felbermayr among the roster fans have followed as the series has grown its international race calendar.

On availability and pricing: Apple announced this as a U.S. service only — fans in the U.S. can watch exclusively on Apple TV beginning in 2027 with a U.S. Apple TV subscription. Apple announced no Canadian availability and no pricing in this article, so CAD pricing is unconfirmed and is not converted here.

What this is — and isn't: this is a confirmed Apple streaming rights announcement dated November 19, 2026, for coverage starting in 2027. It is not a new product, device, or price change, and it does not change current Formula 1 coverage on Apple TV this season.

Apple has announced the finalists for the 2026 App Store Awards.

Apple says global App Store editors selected 45 app and game finalists whose work exemplifies technical innovation, user experience, and design. The finalists span iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Vision Pro, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Apple Arcade, as well as the Cultural Impact category. Winners will be announced in the coming weeks.

“We're excited to celebrate this year's App Store Award finalists, whose creativity has brought extraordinary apps and games to life for users around the world,” said Carson Oliver, Apple's vice president of App Store, in Apple's announcement.

Finalists by category, per Apple:

iPhone App of the Year: ElevenReader, (Not Boring) Camera, Raylie. iPhone Game of the Year: BALL x PIT, DAVE THE DIVER, Gambonanza.

iPad App of the Year: Cosmos, Kiddopia, Mockup. iPad Game of the Year: Aniimo, Arknights: Endfield, Where Winds Meet.

Mac App of the Year: Paste, Things 3, Ulysses. Mac Game of the Year: Big Walk, Blue Prince, Crimson Desert.

Apple Arcade Game of the Year: Perchang World, PowerWash Simulator, Pusheen's Place. Apple Vision Pro App of the Year: Adobe Premiere, MLB, Museas. Apple Vision Pro Game of the Year: Cueva de las Manos, Ping Pong Club, Spatial Ops.

Apple Watch App of the Year: Bevel, Moonlitt, StressWatch. Apple TV App of the Year: Case Solved: The London Files, Letterboxd, Pocket Casts.

Cultural Impact: Brilliant, chilli, Hearing Buddy, Karrot, setlog, and Unedo for apps; and Roger, Consume Me, PancitoMerge, Sago Mini Jinja's Garden, Spilled!, and Tiny Bookshop for games.

What this is — and isn't: this is a confirmed Apple editorial announcement dated November 18, 2026. It is not a new product, price change, or service launch, and Apple announced no pricing or availability changes alongside it. No CAD or US pricing is involved.

stories.article:
AI Tech Update — November 17, 2026

Apple Podcasts has named Baby, this is Keke Palmer its Show of the Year for 2026.

The show is hosted by Keke Palmer and produced by Wondery, with Palmer also serving as executive producer. Apple says the award honours the podcast for its exceptional quality and cultural impact.

According to Apple, the show consistently ranks among the top video and top comedy shows on Apple Podcasts. Recent conversations cited by Apple include Oprah Winfrey on self-worth, and Anderson .Paak on creativity, reinvention, and fatherhood.

“I'm so honored that Baby, this is Keke Palmer has been named Apple Podcasts' Show of the Year,” Palmer said in Apple's announcement.

Oliver Schusser, Apple's vice president of Podcasts, Music, Sports, and Beats, said Palmer's “curiosity, humor, and openness make every conversation feel personal,” and pointed to video as bringing that connection closer.

What this is — and isn't: this is a confirmed Apple editorial award announced November 17, 2026. It is not a new product, price change, or service launch, and Apple announced no pricing or availability changes alongside it.

stories.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix Streams Live on Apple TV This Weekend
stories.summary: Apple has announced that the FORMULA 1® HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX™ 2026 will stream live on Apple TV this weekend.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — November 17, 2026

Apple has announced that the FORMULA 1® HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX™ 2026 will stream live on Apple TV this weekend.

Apple describes it as the final U.S. race of the season and the only night race in the United States, with every session available live and on demand. The article's hero image lists it as “WATCH FREE NOV 21 AT 11PM ET” — Saturday, November 21. The article text itself says only “this weekend” for the race timing.

Apple says the Grand Prix is streaming for free in the U.S. on Apple TV, and also notes that viewers are required to have a U.S. Apple TV subscription. Both points are as Apple states them in the announcement.

Viewers can watch in the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad, Apple TV 4K, Apple Vision Pro, and Mac, on popular smart TVs from Samsung, LG, Sony, VIZIO, TCL, and others, on Roku and Amazon Fire TV devices, Chromecast with Google TV, and PlayStation and Xbox consoles, and at tv.apple.com.

Broadcast details from Apple: English and Spanish commentary, up to 30 additional live feeds across sessions — including Driver Tracker, timing and data feeds, a mixed onboard feed, and a Podium feed following P1, P2, and P3 — plus Multiview with up to four live feeds on one screen, now also on supported smart TVs, and F1 in Dolby Atmos and Dolby Vision on supported devices.

Univision will simulcast Apple TV's broadcast, with race coverage beginning at 10 p.m. ET and pre- and post-race programming for Spanish-speaking audiences. Tubi's The Fast Lane altcast also returns, streaming free on Tubi, hosted by Michelle Khare and Justin Bell.

On pricing, Apple's “How to Watch” section lists F1 on Apple TV at $14.99 per month in the U.S., with a seven-day free trial for new subscribers, and three months of Apple TV free for a limited time with an eligible new iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, or Mac purchase and activation. That is U.S. pricing from Apple's U.S. announcement — Canadian pricing was not provided, so CAD is unconfirmed and is not converted here.

What this is — and isn't: this is a confirmed Apple streaming announcement dated November 17, 2026, for a U.S. broadcast this weekend. It is not a new product or a price change, and Apple announced no Canadian viewing or pricing details in this article.

stories.title: Apple Launches Health AI Study in the U.S. — No Canada Rollout Announced
stories.summary: Apple today announced the Apple Health AI Usage Study, a virtual research study in the United States designed to examine how people interact with conversational health AI tools.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — November 15, 2026

Apple today announced the Apple Health AI Usage Study, a virtual research study in the United States designed to examine how people interact with conversational health AI tools.

According to Apple, the study will evaluate what drives user trust, the quality of responses, comprehension, and everyday health actions, with the aim of informing the responsible design of health AI experiences.

The study is conducted in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform Apple says generates answers using medical information from established sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, the Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. In the study app, participants can ask everyday health questions, explore complex medical information in approachable language, and see linked, peer-reviewed clinical citations for responses. Participants can also choose to share HealthKit data types — such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results — to explore how personal data affects relevance and understanding.

Apple says the study was designed with privacy protections, transparency, and clinical guardrails, and that study data will not be used to train AI models. Participants retain control over whether to share HealthKit metrics or survey responses. The study app includes guardrails intended to detect certain concerning questions and suggest following up with a provider or other resources. Apple also notes the study app is not meant to diagnose or treat any condition, or replace the advice of medical professionals.

Availability — confirmed facts only: open to up to 200,000 eligible participants, age 21 and older, across the United States; requires an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro or later) running iOS 26 or later; enrollment is through the study app.

Pricing: none — this is a research study, not a product. No CAD pricing applies, and no Canadian availability was announced.

Fact check note: this is a confirmed Apple announcement, not a rumour. Apple did not announce a new Health app feature, a consumer AI health product, or a Canadian launch in this release — only the U.S. study itself.

Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple's vice president of Health and Fitness: “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.”

Apple HomeView Is Available Today in Canada — $429 CAD
stories.summary: Apple's HomeView smart display went on sale today, November 13, in Canada and six other launch markets. Both the tabletop and wall-mounted models are $429 CAD. It has a 7-inch Liquid Retina display, Siri AI, and face recognition for up to six people.
stories.article:
Apple HomeView is available starting today, November 13, 2026, at Apple Store locations, on the Apple Store online, and in the Apple Store app. Canada is a launch market, alongside Australia, India, New Zealand, Singapore, the UK, and the U.S. HomeView is not on sale in the European Union — Apple says Siri AI is currently unavailable in iOS in the EU, and that it is working with the EU on a path forward.

HomeView is a smart display built around Siri AI and a 7-inch Liquid Retina display. It handles entertainment, FaceTime calls, and smart home control through the Home app, and it recognizes up to six people by face, showing each person their own content in Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My. Personal content only appears when the recognized person's paired iPhone or iPad is present and was recently unlocked.

There are two models at the same price:

Tabletop — silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray
Wall-mounted — silver and space gray

Both are $429 CAD in Canada ($299 in the U.S.). The wall-mounted model needs a mount, sold separately. Apple's Newsroom announcement lists Schneider Home mounts in U.S. pricing only — Power Mount USB-C from $59.95 US and Power Mount AC Wired from $79.95 US, available today, with a Power Mount PoE Wired version coming in early 2027 at $129.95 US. Canadian pricing for the mounts was not stated in Apple's announcement, so treat it as unconfirmed until Apple Canada lists it.

Siri AI on HomeView is available in English in Canada at launch. Canadian French support comes later through a free software update. Per Apple's fine print, Siri AI on HomeView is in beta in HomeView software version 27.2, and the more personal requests need a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad.

stories.title: Apple TV Adds Sign Language Interpretation, Starting With Being Heumann
stories.summary: Apple has announced a new accessibility feature for the Apple TV app: viewers can watch supported titles with accompanying sign language interpretation.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — November 10, 2026

Apple has announced a new accessibility feature for the Apple TV app: viewers can watch supported titles with accompanying sign language interpretation.

The feature, called Sign Language, debuted on Friday, November 13, 2026, alongside the global streaming premiere of Being Heumann, the film based on the true story of disability rights activist Judy Heumann, directed by Siân Heder and starring Ruth Madeley.

In addition to Being Heumann, interpretation for American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) is available for the movie F1. Apple says Way of the Warrior Kid and Greyhound will follow later this year, with more Apple Original titles to come.

How it works, per Apple: turn the option on in Apple TV app settings, and it appears on supported Apple Original titles; while watching, viewers press the Sign Language button. Titles with interpretation carry a Sign Language icon, search surfaces them with phrases like “with ASL,” and a “Movies & Shows with American Sign Language” collection gathers them in one place.

Apple says the performances are designed and tested by Deaf and native signers, and each is crafted to fit the film it interprets. Daniel Durant, who appears in Being Heumann and directed the film's sign language interpretation, said the work aimed to capture the emotion and meaning of the story.

Requirements (Apple's footnote): the Sign Language feature is available on iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, macOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, and visionOS 27.2 or later, or on supported third-party devices running the latest Apple TV app software.

What this is — and isn't: this is a confirmed Apple accessibility announcement dated November 10, 2026, and the feature is already live as of November 13. It is not a new product or a price change, and Apple announced no pricing alongside it.

Apple Rushed the Duo
stories.summary: Apple's first foldable sold out in minutes. Now, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, we may know why: Apple reportedly rushed the iPhone Duo to market. This is reported news, not Apple's version of events — and the distinction matters for everything that follows.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — November 3, 2026

Apple's first foldable sold out in minutes. Now, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, we may know why: Apple reportedly rushed the iPhone Duo to market. This is reported news, not Apple's version of events — and the distinction matters for everything that follows.

The plan changed: Gurman reports that Apple's original plan was very different. The Duo was supposed to wait until November, and launch only in the United States and China. Instead, it went on sale October 23, in more than 70 countries — a full month early, before Apple had built up enough stock. The Apple Post's earlier reporting fits the same picture: Apple had previously been concerned the Duo could slip into late November because of production challenges. The new Bloomberg detail reframes November not as a worst-case delay, but as the original plan.

The shortage, in numbers: pre-orders opened October 16, and within about 30 minutes, Apple's United States store had moved every configuration to a January 25 delivery estimate. Reports say roughly 80 percent of early stock went straight to physical Apple Stores, which is why walk-in customers had a chance while online buyers waited months. Some carriers quoted earlier December dates, but those estimates kept shifting. Delivery dates are estimates, not promises.

What Apple said: on its earnings call on November 2, Apple did not dispute the demand. Chief Operating Officer Sabih Khan said it is really hard to predict when supply and demand will balance. Chief Executive John Ternus called the Duo the most transformational iPhone since the original, and said Apple is working to get it into customers' hands as quickly as it can. Apple gave no Duo sales numbers on the call, and none are claimed here.

The phone: for context, the Duo is Apple's first foldable phone. It opens like a book, from a 5.4-inch outer display to a 7.6-inch inner display. It uses Touch ID, not Face ID, and runs the A20 Pro chip. It starts at $2,999 CAD ($1,999 US). Part of the supply problem is how hard the phone is to build — Gurman also reports low manufacturing yields, and a hinge assembly with more than a hundred parts.

A question that needs care: some have asked whether the rushed timeline connects to the early reports of inner screens cracking along the hinge. That link is speculation, not a finding, and no evidence says so. What is confirmed: Apple says only a small number of units are affected, has not said what causes the failures, and is replacing affected units through AppleCare. Do not let anyone sell you the rush as the cause of the cracks.

The verdict: Apple got a head start on the holiday season, at the cost of availability. There is still no restock date, and January remains the realistic horizon for online orders. Replacements are scarce too, which makes the early hardware reports harder to resolve. The Duo is a hit Apple could not keep in stock, because — reportedly — it did not give itself time to build enough.

Sources: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman via MacObserver and The Apple Post (November 3, 2026); delivery-estimate reporting via toisthe.com (November 3, 2026); Apple November 2 earnings call. All rushed-launch claims are labelled reported; nothing here is presented as Apple-confirmed. From the Apple, Honestly playlist. Watch the video: “Apple Rushed the Duo” ↗

stories.title: Apple's Record $114.5B Quarter — And Why Christmas Costs More
stories.summary: Apple just posted its biggest September quarter ever — and the stock still slipped after hours. Here's why both of those things are true.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — November 3, 2026

Apple just posted its biggest September quarter ever — and the stock still slipped after hours. Here's why both of those things are true.

On Monday, November 2, 2026, Apple reported fiscal fourth-quarter results for the quarter ended September 26, 2026 — CEO John Ternus's first earnings call, alongside CFO Kevan Parekh. The headline numbers are records. The story underneath them is a margin squeeze.

The beat is real: revenue came in at $114.477 billion US, up 12% from a year ago — a September-quarter record, above Apple's own guidance of 9–11% growth and above the LSEG consensus of $113.39 billion. Earnings per share were $2.10, up 14%, against $1.99 expected. Net income was $30.711 billion. For the full fiscal year, Apple posted a record $478.834 billion in revenue.

The iPhone did it: iPhone revenue hit $57.583 billion, up 17.5% — also a September-quarter record — on just nine days of iPhone 18 Pro sales (the Pro models went on sale September 18). Mac surprised to the upside at $10.792 billion, up 23.7%, the fastest-growing category Apple reports. Services set a record at $31.573 billion. The soft spots: iPad down 10.4% to $6.229 billion, and Wearables, Home and Accessories down 7.9% to $8.300 billion. Greater China grew 21% to $17.539 billion, but came in below the roughly $18.8 billion consensus cited in post-release coverage — the one soft spot in an otherwise beat quarter.

The asterisk, handled honestly: about five cents of earnings per share came from tariff refunds, worth about a point of gross margin (47.9% including refunds). Strip them out and earnings are $2.05 — still above the $1.99 consensus. The beat survives without the refunds. But Apple says it has now received the vast majority of those refunds, so that tailwind is fading, not recurring.

The real story: memory. On the call, Ternus called current memory pricing “unprecedented.” September memory costs ran higher than June's, and stripping tariff refunds out of both quarters, margin fell about a point sequentially — driven entirely by memory. Apple has already raised prices on many products, Mac and iPad at the end of June and iPhone in September, and the fading benefit of cheaper inventory bought earlier will only tighten the squeeze. The cost of ramping up Siri AI adds further pressure. No DRAM-versus-NAND cost split was given on the call, and none is claimed here.

The holiday guide: for the December quarter, Apple guided revenue growth of 7–10% — roughly $153.8–158.1 billion US — with gross margin of 45–46%, down from 47.9%, and Services growth of 8–9%. Apple still expects its best quarter ever. But compare the guide to the right consensus and the picture splits: it sits above Visible Alpha's $153.0 billion December consensus, yet below LSEG's expectation of 11.4% growth (about $160.1 billion). That split is behind the “holiday outlook falls short” headlines.

After hours, Apple shares told the same two-sided story: up to $340.00 on the release, down to $323.33 during the call, settling around $328.81 — down 2.81% after a regular session that closed down 1.83% at $338.32 (all US dollars, Nasdaq; source: 9to5Mac, November 2, 2026).

What to watch in January: the iPhone Duo is not in this quarter at all — it went on sale October 23, after the quarter ended — so January's report is the first real Duo verdict. December includes Duo sales, but Apple baked constrained supply into its guide, so it should not be counted as a guaranteed beat. The other question for January: whether memory costs force Apple to raise prices again.

All earnings figures in this article are in US dollars, as reported by Apple on November 2, 2026. No Canadian-dollar conversion is established for earnings. Consensus figures are labelled by compiler; where a figure is derived rather than Apple-reported (such as earnings excluding tariff refunds), it is labelled as derived. From the Apple, Honestly playlist. Watch the video: “Apple's Record $114.5B Quarter — And Why Christmas Costs More” ↗

stories.title: iPhone Duo Crackgate — What Apple Has Confirmed (and Hasn't)
stories.summary: Three weeks after the first iPhone Duo screens cracked along the fold, the story has grown — but the facts have not all grown at the same rate. Some things Apple has confirmed. Some things are only reported. And some things are still just theories. Keeping those three buckets apart is the whole point of this update.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — November 3, 2026

Three weeks after the first iPhone Duo screens cracked along the fold, the story has grown — but the facts have not all grown at the same rate. Some things Apple has confirmed. Some things are only reported. And some things are still just theories. Keeping those three buckets apart is the whole point of this update.

What Apple has confirmed: on October 26, 2026, Apple said it was aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of Duo units, and told owners to contact AppleCare for a replacement. On October 30, MacRumors reported an internal memo to Apple Stores and authorized service providers: inspect the phone, then repair or replace it under standard procedures. Apple also says most units are not susceptible, and affected units tend to show the defect quickly.

And confirmed: there is no recall, and no public repair program.

What is reported, not confirmed: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says he independently verified cracked Duo displays on phones used normally, and that Apple's “small number” could mean thousands of units. That is Gurman's claim — Apple has still not given a number. Owners report the same sequence: a stiff hinge, then a crunch or pop, then a crack along the hinge.

The theory: the hinge. iFixit's teardown offers two possible explanations, and iFixit itself says they are theories, not a diagnosis. One: a centre support bar in the hinge may not drop far enough as the phone closes, pressing on the display. Two: curved guide rails may rise into the panel. The hinge supplier, Fine M-Tec, denies its parts caused the problem. iFixit also gave the Duo a provisional repairability score of five out of ten, and puts an out-of-warranty inner screen repair at $999 US — half the phone's $1,999 US starting price.

One test is not a verdict: one livestreamed test by Polish reviewer Kuba Klawiter folded a single retail Duo by hand: clean for 50,000 folds, then dust, then ice — and lines appeared at 75,003 folds. Reports differ on whether the hinge or the screen failed. Other tests differ too: a robot test passed 32,640 folds with no deterioration, and a lab machine passed 75,000 and kept going. Apple publishes no fold rating at all.

What owners face now: Apple replaces affected units through AppleCare, and you do not need AppleCare+ for this issue, as reported by 9to5Mac. Carrier customers should go to AppleCare directly. In South Korea, replacement stock is reported short, with new orders shipping in about three months. And American launch-day buyers: Apple's standard 14-day return window ends November 6.

The honest summary: the issue is real — Apple confirmed that. Its scale is still unproven — Apple will not give a number, and Gurman's thousands is a report, not a confirmation. There is no confirmed cause, and no recall. Watch for Apple's next statement, and whether that store memo becomes a public program.

One caution: some viral hinge-failure posts going around are actually Microsoft's Surface Duo, not Apple's. Check the phone before you believe the photo.

The iPhone Duo starts at $2,999 CAD ($1,999 US) and went on sale October 23, 2026. Repair prices in this article are in US dollars, as reported by iFixit. Sources: Apple statement via MacRumors (Oct 26); MacRumors store-memo report (Oct 30); Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Power On (reported Nov 2–3); iFixit teardown (Oct 25); Notebookcheck / iPhone in Canada on the Klawiter fold test (Oct 27); 9to5Mac; AJU Press (Nov 3); Softonic Surface Duo debunk (Nov 3). From the Apple, Honestly playlist. Watch the video: “iPhone Duo Crackgate — What Apple Has Confirmed (and Hasn't)” ↗

stories.title: HomePod mini 2 Is Here — Worth $199 CAD?
stories.summary: What's new: HomePod mini 2 is the first update since 2020. It runs the S10 chip, comes in five colours, and adds Sound Glow, use as a Mac speaker, and full smart-home control as a Home hub. Price: $199 CAD — $398 for a stereo pair.
stories.article:
What's new: HomePod mini 2 is the first update since 2020. It runs the S10 chip, comes in five colours, and adds Sound Glow, use as a Mac speaker, and full smart-home control as a Home hub. Price: $199 CAD — $398 for a stereo pair.

The catch, stated plainly: there is no Siri AI at launch. It's promised as a free update later, with no date given. If Siri AI is the reason you'd upgrade, that feature isn't in the box on day one.

The math: four HomePod mini 2 speakers plus an Apple TV 4K for a surround setup comes to $1,225 CAD — worth knowing before you start with one and drift into four.

So, upgrade or wait? If your original mini is a music speaker and Home hub, the S10 and the new features make launch day — Friday, October 30 — a reasonable buy. If you're waiting on Siri AI, wait for the update; the hardware isn't going anywhere. The full verdict is in the launch-day video.

stories.title: Apple's First Touchscreen Mac Is Here — MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display
stories.summary: It's real, and it's confirmed. On Wednesday, October 28, 2026, Apple announced the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display — its first touchscreen Mac — in 14-inch and 16-inch models. After years of Apple saying touch belonged on iPad, Touch has come to the Mac, and it arrives on the most powerful MacBook Pros Apple has ever made.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — October 28, 2026

It's real, and it's confirmed. On Wednesday, October 28, 2026, Apple announced the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display — its first touchscreen Mac — in 14-inch and 16-inch models. After years of Apple saying touch belonged on iPad, Touch has come to the Mac, and it arrives on the most powerful MacBook Pros Apple has ever made.

The display: a tandem OLED PROLED XDR panel, rated at up to 2,000 nits peak brightness for both HDR and SDR content, with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. ProMotion runs from 10Hz to 120Hz, and the panel covers both the P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts. This is the headline upgrade — OLED on a MacBook Pro for the first time, and brighter than any Mac display before it.

Touch on Mac, and the Dynamic Island: for the first time, you can touch a Mac's screen — tap, swipe and interact directly, alongside the keyboard and trackpad. The notch is gone too: the Dynamic Island has come to the Mac, bringing Live Activities and the camera housing into one interactive area at the top of the display.

The power: M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, configurable with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage, and battery life rated at up to 24 hours. The new design is lighter as well — the 14-inch model weighs 3 pounds, the 16-inch 4 pounds.

Canadian pricing (confirmed by Apple Canada, before tax): the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro starts at $3,999 CAD, and the 16-inch with M5 Pro at $4,799 CAD. Stepping up to M5 Max: $6,299 CAD for the 14-inch and $6,599 CAD for the 16-inch. Education pricing starts at $3,789 / $4,519 / $5,869 / $6,189 CAD. For reference, US starting prices are $2,899 / $3,399 / $4,499 / $4,799 US, in the same order — labelled US, because on this channel Canadian prices lead.

Dates: pre-orders opened today, Wednesday, October 28, 2026, and the new MacBook Pro is available Friday, November 6, 2026 — Canada included.

A quick recap of the week so far: today's touchscreen MacBook Pro is the only new Apple announcement of October 28. The other three products in this week's coverage were announced earlier, on October 26–27: the OLED iPad mini from $949 CAD, the M6 iMac from $2,099 CAD, and the M6 14-inch MacBook Pro from $2,799 CAD. Those are yesterday's news, recapped in our earlier video — not part of today's release.

All facts in this article are confirmed from Apple's newsroom releases of October 28, 2026 (US and Canada). From the Apple, Honestly playlist. Watch the video: “Apple's First Touchscreen Mac Is Here — MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display” ↗

stories.title: Apple Didn't Wait — 3 New Products Before Tomorrow's Event

AI Tech Update — October 27, 2026

Apple didn't wait for its own event. One day before the confirmed “Pro and tell” event on Wednesday, October 28, Apple announced three new products early: the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6, the 24-inch iMac with M6, and the OLED iPad mini with A20 Pro. Pre-orders open October 28, and all three are available Friday, November 6 — Canada included, with Canadian pricing confirmed on each one.

14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 — from $2,799 CAD. The entry MacBook Pro moves to the M6 chip. This is the announcement, with a price attached: $2,799 CAD to start, pre-orders October 28, in stores and shipping November 6.

24-inch iMac with M6 — from $2,099 CAD (10-core) / $2,299 CAD (12-core). The iMac gets M6 in two configurations: the 10-core version starts at $2,099 CAD, and the 12-core version at $2,299 CAD. Same dates as the rest of this drop — pre-orders October 28, availability November 6.

OLED iPad mini with A20 Pro — from $949 CAD Wi-Fi. The iPad mini finally gets an OLED screen, running on the A20 Pro chip, starting at $949 CAD for the Wi-Fi model. Pre-orders open October 28; availability is November 6.

What is still only expected tomorrow: the October 28 “Pro and tell” event itself is confirmed, and it is still happening. The touchscreen OLED MacBook Pros expected there are reported only — not announced. Keep them separate from today's news: the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 announced here is a different machine from the reported touchscreen model, and nothing about today's three announcements confirms it.

From rumour to announcement: two of these three — the M6 Macs and the OLED iPad mini — were covered on this channel as rumours, labelled as rumours. They are announcements now, with confirmed specs and Canadian prices, and this article is written from the announcement. The earlier rumour coverage stays as it was: an honest record of what was reported at the time.

stories.title: iOS 27.2 Is Here — And Your iPhone Skips 27.1
stories.summary: iOS 27.2 is here — Apple released it Monday, October 26, 2026 (build 24B119; 24B91020 on the iPhone Duo). If you were waiting for iOS 27.1, stop: almost every iPhone skipped it.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — October 26, 2026

iOS 27.2 is here — Apple released it Monday, October 26, 2026 (build 24B119; 24B91020 on the iPhone Duo). If you were waiting for iOS 27.1, stop: almost every iPhone skipped it.

Why there's no 27.1 for you: iOS 27.1 exists only on the iPhone Duo, which launched October 23 running 27.1. Apple reportedly kept 27.1 exclusive so the Duo's software stayed under wraps during beta testing. Every other iPhone jumps straight from 27.0.x to 27.2.

What's new in 27.2: Siri AI in five new languages — French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish — with French the big one for Canadian viewers. User profiles in the Apple TV app. Dual Capture for Group FaceTime, filming with the front and rear cameras at the same time. Messages suggestions that turn chat details into calendar events and reminders. An Apple Podcasts Up Next redesign, design tweaks in Books and Music, Call Context anniversary alerts, and a new Apple Music icon. Note: Siri AI features require iPhone 15 Pro or newer; the rest of 27.2 works on other supported iPhones.

The honest twist: the redesigned Health app was in the betas, and Apple pulled it before the release candidate. Apple's RC notes say it will be available again in an upcoming iOS beta — so it is NOT in 27.2 at launch.

Home tie-in: HomePod software 27.2 brings the Siri AI beta to HomeView (on sale November 13) and lands around the HomePod mini 2 launch (October 30).

Watch the video here: https://youtu.be/AxgOfjFuX8o

stories.title: Apple Took Nvidia's Crown — For a Few Hours
stories.summary: Apple is the most valuable company in the world again. Or it was, briefly, on Friday morning — and the honest version of this story is more interesting than the headline. This report was first broken by 9to5Mac on iPhone Duo launch day, and here's what actually happened, with the numbers attached.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — October 23, 2026

Apple is the most valuable company in the world again. Or it was, briefly, on Friday morning — and the honest version of this story is more interesting than the headline. This report was first broken by 9to5Mac on iPhone Duo launch day, and here's what actually happened, with the numbers attached.

During Friday's session, Apple traded above US$351 a share and set a new intraday record high of US$351.73. At its peak, Apple's market value reached roughly US$5.12 trillion (sources tracking the morning put the range between US$5.10 and US$5.13 trillion). At that moment, Nvidia was worth about US$5.06 to US$5.10 trillion — a figure 9to5Mac didn't publish, which comes from other outlets following the session. Later in the same session, Apple eased back and live rankings put Nvidia in front again. The crown changed hands, and then it changed back.

Context matters here. At Thursday's close, Nvidia was still number one at US$5.11 trillion, even after a rough day: its shares fell 4.4 percent to US$212.21, wiping out roughly US$235 billion in value after CEO Jensen Huang's comments at GTC Berlin and Meta's AI spending plans rattled chip stocks. Apple closed second at US$5.08 trillion on a record close of US$348.22. The gap between the two companies was just US$42 billion — 0.83 percent. When the gap is that small, an ordinary good morning is all it takes to flip the ranking.

Three weeks ago, this wasn't close at all. At Nvidia's record close on October 6, its lead over Apple was about US$903 billion. Since then, Apple has risen about 4.3 percent while Nvidia has fallen about 11 percent. Friday's flip was as much about Nvidia sliding as Apple surging.

It helped that Friday was also a product story. The iPhone Duo launched in more than 70 countries starting at US$1,999 (CA$2,999 in Canada). Pre-orders opened on October 16, and delivery estimates slipped to late January 2027 within about half an hour. Apple called demand "nothing short of extraordinary." A sold-out foldable launch is exactly the kind of momentum that carries a stock to a record high.

This rivalry has history. Nvidia became the first company ever to reach US$5 trillion on October 29, 2025. Apple first closed above US$5 trillion on October 14 of this year, and it last closed at number one on July 27, 2026. Since the start of 2024, by Yahoo Finance's calculation, the top spot has swapped roughly two dozen times.

Analysts, for their part, are split — and their views are opinion, not fact. JPMorgan reiterated a US$360 target on Apple on October 19. One day later, Loop Capital downgraded Apple from Buy to Hold and cut its target to US$330. Same stock, same week, opposite calls.

What actually decides the crown is earnings. Apple reports on Monday, November 2 — John Ternus's first earnings call as CEO. That quarter ended September 26, so it contains no Duo sales at all; the number to watch is December-quarter guidance. Nvidia reports in mid-November. Until then, the accurate headline is the modest one: Apple took Nvidia's crown — for a few hours.

Watch the video: "Apple Took Nvidia's Crown — For a Few Hours" on the AI Tech Update YouTube channel. All figures US$ unless noted. Sources: 9to5Mac (original report, Oct 23, 2026), cross-checked against Seeking Alpha, Stocktwits, BigGo Finance, TipRanks and The Apple Post.

Update — market close, Fri Oct 23: Apple's lead lasted only hours. AAPL closed at $347.73 (−0.1%) off its $351.73 intraday record, while Nvidia closed at $210.96 (−0.6%) worth ~$5.11T, retaking the world's-most-valuable crown into the weekend.

stories.title: iPhone Duo Is Here — On Sale Today From $2,999 CAD, Sold Out Into January
stories.summary: Apple's first foldable iPhone went on sale today, Friday, October 23, in Canada and more than 70 countries — starting at $2,999 CAD. Here is what is confirmed, what is merely reported, and what the first reviews actually say.
stories.article:
AI Tech Update — October 23, 2026

Apple's first foldable iPhone went on sale today, Friday, October 23, in Canada and more than 70 countries — starting at $2,999 CAD. Here is what is confirmed, what is merely reported, and what the first reviews actually say.

Confirmed (Apple's published specs and launch details): a book-style foldable with a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display with a matte nano-texture finish. It is 5.2 mm thick when open, weighs 254 grams, and runs on the A20 Pro chip, with IP68 water resistance and MagSafe. Touch ID sits in the side button — there is no Face ID. Colours are Night Sky and Star White. It runs iOS 27.1, a version exclusive to the Duo. Pricing starts at $2,999 CAD (256GB); US pricing runs $1,999–$3,199 (US). Twenty-eight more countries follow on October 30.

Reported (supply and demand): pre-orders opened October 16, and delivery estimates slipped to late January 2027 within minutes, per CNBC, MacRumors and Engadget. Apple called preorder demand "nothing short of extraordinary." Walk-in store stock is limited, and Apple reportedly raised its first-year production target by 44 percent, to 14 million units.

What the reviews say (embargo lifted October 21): Engadget scored it 8.8 out of 10 — "a first-class foldable" — praising the inner screen (the crease is felt more than seen), the titanium build, and battery life of 28 hours 48 minutes in its rundown test, ahead of the Galaxy Z Fold 8. The criticisms are real too: no telephoto lens (the 2x zoom is a sensor crop), a main camera a step below the iPhone 18 Pro, Touch ID instead of Face ID, a cramped cover screen for typing (The Verge), and the phone running warm in video apps (The Verge). Most third-party apps are not yet optimized for the big screen.

The verdict: a genuinely impressive first foldable at a genuinely flagship price — $2,999 CAD is the number to sit with. Watch the full video on the channel for the complete breakdown, and see our Duo 2 Face ID rumour coverage for where Apple reportedly takes this next.

All prices Canadian unless labelled US. Sources: Apple's published iPhone Duo specifications and launch details; supply and demand reporting by CNBC, MacRumors and Engadget; reviews by Engadget, The Verge and 9to5Mac, published October 21, 2026.

stories.title: ChatGPT Rumours: A Reworked Astra, Sol in Chat, and the GPT-6.2 Question
stories.summary: Status first: this is a rumours roundup. Almost everything below is reporting, sightings or chatter — not an OpenAI announcement — and each item is labelled with exactly how solid it is.
stories.article:
Status first: this is a rumours roundup. Almost everything below is reporting, sightings or chatter — not an OpenAI announcement — and each item is labelled with exactly how solid it is.

The confirmed anchor: GPT-6.1 Sol shipped at DevDay on September 29, 2026. GPT-6.1 Astra's October launch was shelved after safety testing. Those two facts are confirmed; everything after this paragraph is not.

Reported — a reworked Astra: reporting points to Astra being reworked and possibly returning. No date has been given for any return, so none is listed here. A shelved model coming back reworked is plausible — it is not a launch plan.

Unconfirmed — Sol in chat: Sol has reportedly been sighted in regular ChatGPT chat. That sighting is unconfirmed: until OpenAI says Sol is in the product, treat it as a spotter's report, not a rollout.

Announced, not live — Sol Ultrafast: this one is different. Sol Ultrafast has been announced, but it is not live yet. Announced is a promise; live is a product — this article keeps the two separate.

Single-source — the “Dots” agents: the “Dots” agents rest on a single source. One source can be right, but on this site a single-source claim gets flagged as single-source until something corroborates it.

Noise — GPT-6.2: GPT-6.2 is presented as noise. There is no credible reporting behind it — no sourcing, no corroboration, nothing to check. It is named here only so you know it was weighed and set aside, not because it carries any weight.

How to hold all of it: one confirmed anchor (Sol shipped, Astra shelved), two reported items with caveats (Astra's return, Sol in chat), one announced-but-not-live item (Sol Ultrafast), one single-source flag (Dots), and one piece of noise (GPT-6.2). If any of it firms up into an announcement, this article gets rewritten around the announcement — until then, the rumour labelling stays on.
